# Expression language evaluated from HTTP request data (Java)

`qualor:java/expression-injection` · Issue · Severity: High · [CWE-917](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/917.html) · OWASP Top 10: [A05:2025 Injection](https://top10.owasp.org/2025/A05_2025-Injection/), [A03:2021 Injection](https://top10.owasp.org/2021/A03_2021-Injection/)

## What it finds

<!-- begin: what-it-finds -->
HTTP request data evaluated as an expression (Jakarta Servlet, Spring MVC, Jakarta REST):

- Spring SpEL: an expression parsed from request data and evaluated with the default
  `StandardEvaluationContext` (`getValue()`, `setValue()`, `getValueType()`);
- Jakarta Expression Language: `ELProcessor.eval()` / `getValue()` and `ExpressionFactory`;
- OGNL and MVEL expressions.
<!-- end: what-it-finds -->

## Why it matters

<!-- begin: why-it-matters -->
These expression languages can call methods, create objects and reach any class, for example
`T(java.lang.Runtime).getRuntime().exec('...')` in SpEL. A client who writes the expression runs
code on the server.
<!-- end: why-it-matters -->

## Example

<!-- begin: example -->
**Noncompliant:** a formula from the client is evaluated with the default context.

```java
package com.example.calc;

import org.springframework.expression.ExpressionParser;
import org.springframework.expression.spel.standard.SpelExpressionParser;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.GetMapping;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RequestParam;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RestController;

@RestController
public class CalcController {
    private final ExpressionParser parser = new SpelExpressionParser();

    @GetMapping("/calc")
    public Object calc(@RequestParam String formula) {
        return parser.parseExpression(formula).getValue();
    }
}
```

**Compliant:** the formula is evaluated with a `SimpleEvaluationContext`, which allows no type
references, constructors or bean references.

```java
package com.example.calc;

import org.springframework.expression.EvaluationContext;
import org.springframework.expression.ExpressionParser;
import org.springframework.expression.spel.standard.SpelExpressionParser;
import org.springframework.expression.spel.support.SimpleEvaluationContext;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.GetMapping;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RequestParam;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RestController;

@RestController
public class CalcController {
    private final ExpressionParser parser = new SpelExpressionParser();

    @GetMapping("/calc")
    public Object calc(@RequestParam String formula) {
        EvaluationContext context = SimpleEvaluationContext.forReadOnlyDataBinding().build();
        return parser.parseExpression(formula).getValue(context);
    }
}
```
<!-- end: example -->

## How to fix

<!-- begin: how-to-fix -->
- Evaluate only expressions the application owns, and pass request data as a variable or value:
  `context.setVariable("name", value)` in SpEL, `defineBean(...)` in Jakarta EL, a context entry in
  OGNL.
- If users must write SpEL expressions, evaluate them with a `SimpleEvaluationContext`
  (`SimpleEvaluationContext.forReadOnlyDataBinding().build()`), never the default
  `StandardEvaluationContext`.
<!-- end: how-to-fix -->

## Frameworks and APIs covered

- Jakarta Servlet
- Spring MVC
- Jakarta REST (JAX-RS)
- Spring Expression Language (SpEL)
- Jakarta Expression Language
- OGNL
- MVEL

## Known limits

<!-- begin: known-limits -->
- A handler parameter without an annotation is not a source (the Jakarta REST entity parameter, a
  Spring MVC simple-type parameter), and enum, `List` or `Optional` parameters still count as
  request data.
- One method is analysed at a time and conditions are not evaluated: a helper of the same class
  that returns a constant still passes request data on, and a wrapper class that reads the request
  is not a source.
- SpEL and OGNL are reported where the expression is evaluated: one parsed in one method and
  evaluated in another is missed. A `SimpleEvaluationContext` is recognised by its type or when
  built in the same method; one returned by a helper is not, so the evaluation is reported.
- Allow-list lookups are recognised only as `Map.of(...)` of constants and as `valueOf` of an enum
  declared in the same file.
<!-- end: known-limits -->

The test file [`rules/java/expression/expression-injection.java`](../../../rules/java/expression/expression-injection.java) holds every case the rule reports or accepts:
lines marked `ruleid:` must be reported and lines marked `ok:` must not. The known limits are
marked `todoruleid:` (missed) and `todook:` (wrongly reported). `npm test` runs them with OpenGrep,
